mainEntity.name: Why is my website not showing up on Google?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google does not guarantee that it will crawl, index or serve every page. Common causes are a noindex tag, a robots.txt file that blocks Google, a page Google has not found, duplicate versions of the page, or content missing on the mobile version.

mainEntity.name: How do I check if my website is indexed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Search your business name and city, then search site:yourwebsite.com. The site: list is not always exhaustive, so use the URL Inspection tool in Search Console to check an individual page.

mainEntity.name: Does a sitemap make Google index my pages?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A sitemap gives Google information about your pages, but Google says it does not guarantee that all the items in it will be crawled and indexed.

mainEntity.name: Can robots.txt remove a page from Google?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says robots.txt is not a mechanism for keeping a web page out of Google. To keep a page out, block indexing with noindex or password-protect the page.

mainEntity.name: If my page is indexed, will it show up in search results?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Google says that just because a page is indexed does not guarantee that it will show up in your search results. Indexing makes a page eligible, and other factors decide whether it appears.
